533: People who are careless and forgetful never become famous. The writers of every kind of book in the world agree on this.
539: Whenever you feel carried away by your own happiness, remember the people who were ruined because they got careless.
552: When a king, who has the power to punish, asks his people for money, it is like a robber with a spear on a lonely road saying, “Hand it over.”
562: Rulers who want to stay successful for a long time should raise the stick sternly but bring it down gently. They should warn firmly but punish mildly.
564: A king whose people call him “our harsh ruler” will have his life cut short and will quickly be destroyed.
565: The great riches of a ruler who is hard to meet and who greets people with an unfriendly face are like treasure guarded by a demon. They are scary and help no one.
591: Inner drive is the only thing a person can truly be said to own. People without it do not really own anything, whatever else they have.
629: A person who does not chase after pleasure in good times will not be crushed by sadness in bad times.
645: Say what you have to say only after making sure that no one can say something that beats your words.
